test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Refer to the given series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only, and all counting is to be done from left to right).

(Left) 1 2 8 2 4 1 7 6 1 7 3 2 9 7 5 1 7 8 6 8 2 4 3 9 4 6 6 2 (Right)

How many such odd digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by a perfect square and immediately followed by an even digit? (Note: 1 will be considered as a perfect square.)
solution:
Given series:

(Left) 1 2 8 2 4 1 7 6 1 7 3 2 9 7 5 1 7 8 6 8 2 4 3 9 4 6 6 2 (Right)

Condition to be checked:

perfect square → odd digits → even digit

(Left) 1 2 8 2 4 __**1 7 6**__ 1 7 3 2 9 7 5 __**1 7 8**__ 6 8 2 4 3 9 4 6 6 2 (Right)

Thus there are two such patterns (1 7 6, __1 7 8__) that are following the above conditions.

Hence,**"2"** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e085a7f17645c801966c030eb44d69fae944b96fdb4c4077f5fba1bc2c24bc71.png] __Mistake Point__

Immediately preceded by means immediately before or to come just before.

Immediately followed by means immediately after or to come just after.
